page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by a custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features an AWS Graviton processor using the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture, operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance in multi-core and single-core computational tasks, with stress-ng scores of 6055.75 and 1520.19 respectively. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is moderate, measuring 63.9 GB/sec for read-only operations and 30.56 GB/sec for write operations. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in memory-bound small block reads and single-threaded compression tasks. Cryptographic operations benefit from hardware-accelerated AES support, though database operations and Redis SET performance fall into the average to weak range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m6gd.xlarge leverages the ARM64 architecture to deliver a balanced ratio of compute and memory resources alongside high-speed local NVMe storage. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring low-latency local scratch space without the overhead of network-attached storage. The instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and database operations that can utilize the local SSD, while it is less optimal for intensive LLM inference or heavy single-threaded decompression tasks.
